compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Discovered while diagnosing the 2026-07-31 `rebar-autodeploy-errors` alarm (root cause filed
separately as 304e-9c0f-2068-4d0e). Two independent weaknesses in the deploy's health gate turned a
recoverable stall into an hour of repeated rollbacks that could not be diagnosed from the deploy
journal alone.

**1. The timeout is below the real worst case.** `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:50` sets
`HEALTH_TIMEOUT="${HEALTH_TIMEOUT:-30}"` and :232 uses it as the readiness deadline. On 2026-07-31 the
review-bot needed **~62s** to become ready, because `run_ensures()` burns a 60s lock budget
(`_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=30` x `_DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS=2`) before giving up and continuing. The container was
killed at +30s and rolled back to `:prev` seven consecutive times — and each rolled-back container
then became healthy ~30s later, proving the image was fine and only the deadline was wrong.

Note the interaction: even after 304e is fixed, any future startup path that legitimately exceeds 30s
will be rolled back rather than waited for. The deploy's deadline should exceed the application's own
internal budgets, not sit below them.

**2. `bot-unhealthy` discards the evidence.** :235 emits
`err bot-unhealthy "review-bot failed health check after deploy; ROLLING BACK to :prev"` and nothing
else. The container's own stderr — which held the decisive signal (the missing `ensure ...` sweep
lines and a 61s gap) — was only recoverable by going to the host and reading `docker logs` for a
container that had already been replaced. The deploy journal alone could not distinguish "image is
broken" from "image is fine but slow", which are opposite remediations.

## Approach

Raise `HEALTH_TIMEOUT` above the application's worst-case cold start, keeping it an env-overridable
default. On a health-check failure, capture and log a bounded tail of the failing container's stderr
into the deploy journal before rolling back, so the next occurrence is diagnosable without host
access.

## Scope

- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` — the `HEALTH_TIMEOUT` default (:50), the readiness loop (:232), and
  the `bot-unhealthy` error path (:235).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `HEALTH_TIMEOUT`'s default exceeds the review-bot's worst-case cold start, with the chosen value
      justified against the application's own internal budgets (notably the ensure-sweep lock budget)
      rather than picked arbitrarily; still overridable by env.
- [ ] A `bot-unhealthy` failure records a bounded tail of the failing container's stderr in the deploy
      journal, so "broken image" and "slow start" are distinguishable from the journal alone.
- [ ] The rollback-to-`:prev` behaviour and the fail-safe guarantee (last-known-good stays live) are
      unchanged; verified by a test or a documented dry run.
compiled_state.title: Autodeploy HEALTH_TIMEOUT=30 is below the review-bot's worst-case cold start, and bot-unhealthy logs no container stderr
